title: Tanzanian Street Samosa
community: Urban Tanzania — the street sambusa at every corner
author: Chef Jabir
desc: Tanzanian Street Sambusa — the crispy triangular pastries sold at every corner, market stall, and bus station across Tanzania. Filled with spiced minced beef, onion, and coriander, sealed and fried until golden. Fast, cheap, and completely addictive.
longDesc: Street sambusa is one of Tanzania's most widely sold street foods — the 500-shilling snack that fuels the country between meals. The street version uses thinner, crispier pastry than the restaurant version and a more assertively spiced filling that holds up to the price point.
ingredients: // Sealing paste: 2 tbsp flour + 2 tbsp water
steps: Make filling: fry onions, garlic, ginger, chilli. Add minced beef. Brown and break up. Add spices and coriander. Cook until completely dry. Cool.
Make pastry: combine flour, salt, oil, water to a stiff dough. Knead 5 minutes. Rest 15 minutes.
Roll very thin. Cut into 10cm circles or squares.
Fold into a cone shape. Fill with a heaped teaspoon of filling.
Seal the top with flour-water paste, pressing firmly.
Fry in batches of 6—8 for 4 minutes until deep golden.
chefTips: The filling must be completely dry — any moisture makes pastry soggy.
The sealing paste must be pressed firmly — oil entry ruins the sambusa.
Fry at 175°C — too hot burns before crisping; too cold means greasy result.
cookingScience: See KEN230 for samosa pastry cooking science. Street sambusa uses a slightly stiffer dough than restaurant versions — this produces a crispier, more rigid crust that stays crunchy longer at street food temperatures.
storage: Freeze uncooked 2 months. Fry from frozen.
culturalNote: Street sambusa is the snack Tanzania runs on — the 500-shilling triangle that bridges the gap between meals, eaten at bus stations, at office doors, between classes. It is as fundamental to Tanzanian street food as the jiko.
